its queued tasks wait without erroring or parking, and a second project\\u0027s tasks are claimable up to the node ceiling\u0022,\u0022A cap of 0 pauses the project - no new claims while existing runs finish naturally - and h9k status shows an unmissable line when ready tasks are held behind a cap of 0 while the node has idle capacity, naming the project, the count held, and the lever; the daemon never unpauses on its own\u0022,\u0022Caps are ceilings, not reservations - nothing is set aside for an idle project, and a project whose cap exceeds its share simply fills whatever the node and other projects\\u0027 activity leave available\u0022,\u0022Every deferred claim is visible with its reason - the daemon log and the waiting task\\u0027s h9k status phrasing both name which limit held it back (project cap N of N vs node N of N) so queue states never need reconstructing\u0022,\u0022The setting is denominated in runs to match the node-level max-concurrent-task-runs from the concurrency-units task, changes take effect on the next dispatch cycle without a daemon restart, and any previously recorded session-denominated per-project value migrates or is retired with the migration named in the command output\u0022,\u0022Interactive claims (h9k task work) count against no project cap, consistent with their zero-run rule at the node level\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Brian\\u0027s token-budget lever (2026-08-29), reframed by the concurrency-units and scheduling rulings (2026-08-30, epic: node capacity and scheduling): h9k project set --max-parallel exists today but is recorded and displayed only; nothing enforces it. The wanted behavior is dispatcher enforcement in the runs denomination.\\n\\nSemantics settled in refinement: a per-project cap is a CEILING (how many at once), never a reservation or a share. Cap 0 is PAUSE - deliberate and sticky, for a project that is broken, budget-frozen, or shelved; the self-releasing \\u0022focus on A first\\u0022 behavior belongs to the priority tier in the cross-project ordering task, not to caps. The pause footgun (a forgotten cap-0 project idling the node) is answered with visibility, not automation: status says what is held and why, the human decides.\\n\\nMotivation unchanged: pacing token spend. A project capped at 1 serializes its work so a week\\u0027s allocation spreads across the week; in the multi-project future, caps let one project idle-throttle while another takes the slots. Not a token reducer, a token pacer - the same work costs the same total.\\n\\nOrdering: after the concurrency-units task (max-concurrent-task-runs at the node) so the denomination exists to match; alongside the cross-project ordering task in the same epic.\u0022},\u0022BlockedBy\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Type\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022},\u0022Model\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022RevisedAt\u0022:\u00222026-08-30T13:44:31.119014\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022RevisedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022EpicId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022QueuePriority\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageComposition\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageCompositionAcknowledged\u0022:false,\u0022ClearInteractiveMode\u0022:false,\u0022StackedOnTaskId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022StackedOnPullRequestNumber\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022CloseLinkedIssue\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022SpikeKind\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ExitCriterion\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Constraints\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false}}","originEventId":"866077e7-10ef-4011-a812-eb83104bd2d4","originSequence":10036,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-08-30T13:44:31.128215+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a052e2-b5e5-75dd-8a77-c90384625a30","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskRevised","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a052e2-b5e5-75dd-8a77-c90384625a30\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022\\u0022Free run slots are allocated across projects by round-robin with an optional priority tier: the longest-unserved project with ready work under its cap wins the next slot (oldest task first within it), a project set to a higher priority outranks the rotation while it has work and releases itself the moment its queue drains, nothing ever preempts a live run, and every claim logs a one-sentence reason naming why that project won\\u0022\u0022},\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022Under contention, free slots rotate - the eligible project longest-unserved since its last dispatch wins the next slot, with oldest assignment first within the project, and a project only holds multiple slots when no other eligible project has ready work\u0022,\u0022Eligibility means ready work under every applicable limit - a project at its own cap, at cap 0, or with nothing assigned is skipped by the rotation without consuming a turn\u0022,\u0022h9k project set --priority (default normal) makes a higher-tier project win every free slot over lower tiers while it has eligible work, with rotation applying within a tier; when the higher tier\\u0027s queue drains the lower tiers resume with no operator action - focus is self-releasing, in contrast to the cap-0 pause\u0022,\u0022Nothing preempts - ordering decides only who receives the next free slot, and a live run always completes regardless of priority or rotation changes made mid-flight\u0022,\u0022Every claim logs one plain sentence naming the winner and why (longest unserved, or priority high), and every deferral names what held the task back, so any dispatch decision is explainable from the log alone\u0022,\u0022With one project on the node the behavior is indistinguishable from today - rotation with a single member is oldest-first, and no new setting is required for the single-project install\u0022,\u0022Tie-breaks are stable and documented (first dispatch on a cold start, equal-priority equal-age ties), so two operators reading the same state predict the same next claim\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022## Background\\n\\nToday the dispatcher has no cross-project ordering concept: assignment is the go signal and the human has been the scheduler. With multiple projects holding standing queues against a small node run budget (max-concurrent-task-runs of 1 or 2), \\u0022who gets the next free slot\\u0022 needs an answer that is fair by default, expressive when the operator has a focus, and explainable per decision.\\n\\n## Design rulings from refinement (Brian, 2026-08-30, epic: node capacity and scheduling)\\n\\n1. **Round-robin is the default.** Longest-unserved project wins, oldest task within it. Zero configuration, starvation-proof, each decision explains itself in one sentence. Chosen over oldest-first-project-blind (a burst wave to one project would starve the other behind the whole wave) and over weighted fair share (proportional mixing needs deficit-counter explanations that fight the one-sentence-reason ethic, and is fleet machinery for a personal node).\\n2. **Priority tier for focus, distinct from cap-0 pause.** \\u0022Drain A first, then continue with B\\u0022 is priority: self-releasing when A empties, nothing to remember. \\u0022Never run B\\u0022 is a cap of 0 on the ceilings task: deliberate and sticky. The two levers are documented against each other so neither is used for the other\\u0027s job.\\n3. **Acted-out semantics to preserve.** Node 2, projects A and B both under-cap with work: stable 1-and-1 split, alternating; a project reaches beyond one slot only when the other has nothing. Node 1: strict task-by-task alternation; a five-task wave on A with one task on B runs A, B, A, A, A, A - the lone task cuts in at the first slot boundary rather than waiting behind the wave. Caps express entitlement-when-alone, not share-under-contention.\\n4. **Explainability is a hard requirement**, matching the dispatcher\\u0027s existing stays-queued logging: the reason rides the claim, not a scheduler state dump.\\n\\n## Ordering\\n\\nAfter the concurrency-units task (node max-concurrent-task-runs) and the per-project ceilings task (db715c8c), whose limits define this task\\u0027s eligibility rules. Same establishes\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022## Background\\n\\nTwo related findings from operating the platform, diagnosed live on 2026-08-30.\\n\\nFirst, the node ceiling is denominated in agent sessions (maxConcurrentAgentSessions), but a run reserves its peak of 2 sessions at admission for its whole life, so the setting has dead values: 3 admits exactly what 2 admits (one run). The operator who designed the system set 3 expecting three units of concurrency and got one.\\n\\nSecond, the slot reservation is bookkeeping, not live agents: a run spawns 1 agent during build, 2 only during the two-lens review passes, 1 during fix and verify sessions, and 0 during verification gates. The whole-life reservation exists only to make admission arithmetic safe.\\n\\n## Design rulings (Brian, 2026-08-30)\\n\\n1. **The node setting is task runs, named max-concurrent-task-runs.** How many task executions are live is the thing the operator actually reasons about; session arithmetic moves inside the daemon. Naming ruling (Brian, 2026-08-30): the compound \\u0022task runs\\u0022 was chosen over bare \\u0022runs\\u0022 (does not say what runs) and over \\u0022max-tasks-in-flight\\u0022 (reads well but \\u0022in flight\\u0022 appears nowhere else in the platform\\u0027s vocabulary, while \\u0022run\\u0022 is the domain\\u0027s first-class term for one execution of one task); the project-level ceiling uses the same words so the term is learned once.\\n2. **A second knob caps sessions within one run.** Global default 3, hardcoded as the default value of a durable global setting; a per-task CLI override can raise or lower it ad hoc, even mid-run. With the two knobs, runs=1 plus cap=1 is a strict-serial maximum-throttle mode, and the total possible live sessions on a node is runs x cap, emergent rather than configured.\\n3. **Cap 1 means serialized lenses.** The two-lens phases dispatch one lens at a time. This throttles burn RATE, not total tokens - the same reviews run, spread over more wall clock - and the task records that distinction so nobody mistakes it for a savings lever.\\n4. **Default 3 is deliberate headroom.** Nothing today spawns a third concurrent session within a run; the room is for future machinery (for example a quick side-session dispatched alongside a fix session - discussed, explicitly not in scope here).\\n5. **Reservation dissolves.** With admission counting runs, the whole-life 2-session reservation is no longer needed as a concept; phases spawn what they need up to the run\\u0027s cap.\\n6. **Concurrency within a run is bounded by coded capability, not agent request.** The daemon only ever spawns sessions for activities it has coded logic for, and agents never ask the daemon for a generic sibling session - they signal a waypoint through the CLI (\\u0022this activity is ready to start\\u0022) and the daemon decides dispatch, the same compose/execute discipline the Jira write surface uses. The per-run cap is therefore the ceiling on simultaneous coded activities for one task: today the daemon knows exactly two that can overlap (the review lenses), so effective concurrency is 2 by construction, and each unit above 2 becomes reachable only when a new overlappable activity is coded into the daemon with its own dispatch logic, stream events, and prompt surface. Free-form helper work inside a slot is already covered by the agent\\u0027s own in-process sub-agents, which the daemon neither sees nor governs.\\n\\n## Implementation notes\\n\\n- The dispatch log already reasons in runs (\\u0022at most N resident agent session(s), which is M live run(s) at 2 session(s) each\\u0022) - this promotes the derived M to the configured value.\\n- Config precedence (backlog 59): env var outranks config file outranks built-in default; the new keys join the same chain.\\n- The serialization path (cap 1) is the only behavior-bearing change and deserves focused tests: lens order, findings merge, severity disposition, oscillation/conformance cap counting, and rulings-carry-forward must be indistinguishable from a parallel pass\\u0027s output
